metaDescription: kitten vaccine schedule: timing table, what to do if a dose is late, and reminders before boosters are due.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters
paragraphs: This kitten plan sequences doses against panleukopenia risk, not against a vague “sometime this season” intention for your cat.

Milestone labels on the kitten table (8 weeks; 12 weeks; 16 weeks; 16 weeks) are operational deadlines for daycare, boarding, travel, and multi-pet intros — a nearly finished kitten kitten series is still incomplete.

If your household also wrestles with multi-cat household exposure or felv risk assessment, put those constraints on the same calendar thread as the FVRCP booster so one reminder system owns the kitten week.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Call the clinic with product names and prior dates the day you notice a missed kitten dose; catch-up timing depends on age and gap length for this cat scenario.
Until the kitten series is current again, reduce the exposure pattern that matches panleukopenia risk, and do not wait for an annual wellness slot to ask about a kitten make-up dose.
After the visit, enable 7-, 3-, and 1-day nudges for the next FVRCP booster due date so the same kitten miss cannot hide inside a shared family calendar.

faqs.question: Is this kitten vaccine schedule a prescription?
faqs.answer: No. It is an editorial planning table aligned with common AAHA/AAFP-style windows and facility patterns. Your veterinarian sets the legal and medical plan for the individual cat.

faqs.question: What if we already missed a date on this kitten schedule?
faqs.answer: Contact the clinic for catch-up timing. Bring prior records, limit high-risk exposure tied to panleukopenia risk, and reset reminders as soon as the next kitten due date is known.

faqs.question: How do reminders help with FVRCP booster?
faqs.answer: PetClues can nudge you 7, 3, and 1 day before that kitten booster is due so boarding and travel deadlines stop arriving as surprises.
